messages:
maria-cs: FYI customer (acme) just escalated — streaming reconnects mid-request, then they get partial output twice and see double billing. Logs attached from their side.

acme-sre: Repro steps: open SSE stream -> send prompt with long output -> auth token rotates (we use session rotation) -> client reconnects -> final chunk missing then later duplicate tokens appended. Billing shows two completion events.

sam-support: Oof. Thanks for the heads up. Do we have the server-side request IDs and the customer's SDK snippet? Can you paste their request headers and an example trace?

acme-sre: Here are the headers and trace we captured:
```
GET /v1/streams?model=orca-13b HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer rlx_XXXX (rotated midstream)
X-Client-Req: a1b2c3

[stream event] seq=0 data: {"token":"Hi"}
[stream event] seq=1 data: {"token":" there"}
[disconnect] code=1006 after seq=120
[reconnect] handshake ok, resume_seq=120
[stream event] seq=121 data: {"token":"!"}
[stream event] seq=121 data: {"token":"!"}
```

maria-cs: They say resume_seq is 120 but the server sent 121 twice. They also saw two billing records for req a1b2c3 with different server request ids.

ingrid-devex: Do we know whether the SDK is using iterators that de-duplicate by seqnum? In past bugs the py iterator accepted duplicates when a token boundary fell on recon. What SDK/version are they on?

acme-sre: python SDK 0.9.3 (pip), using the streaming iterator example from the docs.

sam-support: @tariq can you look at runtime logs for tenant acme around 2026-03-16T14:02Z? We should check resume handshake logic and billing dedupe window.

 deploy-bot: deploy event: inference-runtime v2.14.0 rolled to region-us-east-1 at 2026-03-16T13:58:21Z (build d9f7).

tariq-eng-runtime: Looking now. I can see a resume handshake where client supplies resume_seq=120. The routing layer accepted it and forwarded to a new backend instance. The backend's streaming generator started at 121 but it replayed one token due to cache insertion race. There's a note in the log: 
```
2026-03-16T14:02:10Z handler: resume_seq=120 -> backend_start_seq=121 (cache_insertion=true)
2026-03-16T14:02:10Z kvcache: insert token @121 succeeded
2026-03-16T14:02:10Z output: emit token seq=121 source=replay
2026-03-16T14:02:10Z output: emit token seq=121 source=newgen
```

chris-ml: That looks like a KV cache race where both replay and live generation produced the same token. We should guard so we never emit duplicate seq numbers to the client. SDKs should also ignore duplicates if they arrive, but server must be canonical.

ingrid-devex: For the python SDK 0.9.3, there was a known iterator change in 0.9.2->0.9.4 that made it yield any incoming chunk rather than dedupe by seq. That would explain the duplicate delivery. But billing double-counting implies the control plane recorded two completions. Are there two finalization events?

acme-sre: Billing shows two records: server_req_id d1f and d1f-retry. Looks like the control plane treated the reconnect as a separate request because the resume token wasn't fully validated.

sam-support: Action items: (1) tariq, add server-side guard to collapse duplicate seq emits in the stream layer and ensure resume handshake only resumes without creating a new billing event. (2) ingrid/chris: patch SDK iterator to dedupe by seq and ignore exact-duplicate tokens. (3) support: ask customer to upgrade to python SDK 0.9.5 when available and provide a short repro snippet.

tariq-eng-runtime: I'll open an internal ticket and attach logs. Quick mitigation: set backend to prefer replay-only on resume until we verify cache insertion ordering.

ingrid-devex: Repro snippet for customer to try (minimal):
```python
from redwood import StreamsClient
client = StreamsClient(token="rlx_xxx")
with client.streams.open(model="orca-13b") as s:
    s.send("long prompt...")
    for chunk in s:
        print(chunk['token'])
# if you see duplicate tokens with same seq, ctrl-c and capture trace
```

chris-ml: Also add a small patch to SDK that keeps a last_seen_seq and drops any incoming chunk where seq <= last_seen_seq (but still accepts noncontiguous jumps for missed tokens). We'll push 0.9.5 with that change.

maria-cs: I told customer we'll prioritize a patch and share ETA. They've paused production traffic. They asked whether this could also cause content corruption (they had one case where last sentence truncated).

tariq-eng-runtime: Duplicate tokens shouldn't corrupt content order but could cause repeats. Truncation likely due to missing final frame on the reconnect path — that's separate and we'll investigate the handshake finalization race.

sam-support: Thanks team. I'll keep ACME updated and request logs after they test 0.9.5. Will follow up when we have a rollback/mitigation plan. :thumbsup:

acme-sre: Appreciate the quick triage. Please keep me posted.
